findings.reason: A quotient-coordinate square materially clarifies the common construction of every W-indexed Bruhat cell from its double coset and explains why the B-factor disappears. The locally supplied facts support this picture directly; a closure-order schematic would require additional incidence results not established here.
findings.action: Appended final Remarks containing a commuting tikzcd quotient square and explanations of its maps, root indexing, dimensions and identity/longest boundary cases.

correction: Added a diagram U_w times B -> Bn_wB over U_w -> C_w, with horizontal isomorphisms, vertical right-B quotient maps, and the exact inverse-root indexing convention. All old source bytes are an unchanged prefix.

diagram_math_checks.result: For every fixed w in the finite W, C_w is the locally closed B-orbit pi_B(Bn_wB), not its closure. mu_w:U_w x B -> Bn_wB is (u,b) -> un_wb and is an isomorphism by F2 and supplier lem-semisimple-bruhat-double-cosets steps 7.1-8.1. pr_1 has target U_w; the right vertical arrow is pi_B restricted with codomain C_w. phi_w:U_w -> C_w is u -> un_wB, the quotient isomorphism established in step 4.1 using the local flag torsor charts.

pi_B(mu_w(u,b)) = un_wbB = un_wB = phi_w(pr_1(u,b)); the equality holds as regular morphisms because the quotient map is right-B-invariant. Horizontal sim labels assert only the proved isomorphisms. Vertical arrows are quotient projections under the coordinates of F2. No inclusion, pullback label, closure incidence or boundary attachment is asserted.

The coordinate roots are I_w = Phi^+ intersect w Phi^-, equivalently positive alpha with w^{-1}alpha negative. They correspond to N(w^{-1}) in def-length-and-longest-element-of-a-finite-weyl-group, not generally N(w). The inversion bijection and equality of inverse lengths in prop-weyl-length-equals-positive-root-inversion-number F/L3, together with double-coset supplier step 10.1, give |I_w|=ell(w). Thus the lower two objects are affine spaces of dimension ell(w), as target step 4.1 states.

Target step 2.1 gives the finite disjoint union X_B = coproduct C_w and step 3.1 gives local closedness. For e, I_e is empty and n_e lies in T, so C_e={B}. For w_0, w_0 sends all positive roots negative and I_w0=Phi^+, yielding dimension |Phi^+|; steps 1.2, 3.2 and 5.1 identify C_w0 with n_w0 pi_B(U^-B), open dense. In the zero-rank case the two named indices coincide and both descriptions give the point; no distinctness is asserted.
The original complete proof is retained byte-for-byte before final Remarks. All figure relations are consequences of existing numbered steps and local suppliers; no proof step invokes the figure.
